# jack/scott weekly
Date: 2026-10-26 | Duration: 32.560001373291016m

## Summary
The team agreed to move forward with Huck Finch using a 100-hour punch card costing under $10,000, while deferring events-page work because Lindsey’s bandwidth is constrained and the Focus Lab project is prioritized. Performance work will add bandwidth, include CMS work, and leave Yousef’s contract unchanged until completion is reviewed. Marketing responsibilities are shifting, with Jacqueline taking paid work and field support under consideration. Analytics ownership is consolidating, with Scott shepherding architecture, Lindsay handling much of the execution, and shared source-of-truth definitions. GrowthBook needs marketing-site instrumentation and product-web alignment; ClickHouse will centralize data, while Hex is preferred for initial prototypes. Product updates shipped successfully, balancing Jack’s preference for faster releases with Scott’s focus on quality, and updates may support sales enablement. An AI workflow prototype embeds Claude with Slack, calendars, email, Notion, Obsidian, and handwritten notes, though prioritization and access remain concerns. Heavy meetings limit deep work, and Jack’s vacation begins after Monday.

# jack/scott weekly
Date: 2026-11-12 | Duration: 32.27000045776367m

## Summary
The discussion covered testing a thirty-foot Class C motorhome, stopping an extension-cord power test after detecting a burning smell, and postponing a several-thousand-dollar dedicated pedestal until functionality is confirmed. The RV may serve as an ADU for relative housing, an office, or a playroom. A Slack app using Claude Code is functionally working, Emmy received the project files, and API-key funding was avoided, but Markdown rendering, channel ordering, and image support remain awkward; development paused after the side-project budget ended. Slack’s role was questioned in favor of Clog, asynchronous communication, human-written messages, and AI-assisted triage with summaries. A synthetic demo environment on Fly.io uses ClickHouse, randomized experiments, deterministic data, and automated resets, while production demos remain blocked by exposed customer names and downgraded permissions. Marketing personas showed little improvement over Claude responses, prompting interest in customer-call data. AI work also includes an AWS re:Invent one-pager, Fable orchestration, Soul Ultra, multiple Codex tasks, and uncertain continued OpenAI access tied to an invitation.

## Keywords
Slack AI integration, Claude Code, Synthetic demo environment, Cluster-randomised experiments, Synthetic personas, AI agent orchestration
